elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered Article XXII deletes the disclosure-plus-five-business-day matching mechanic entirely and states that Licensee may transact "without notice to, or any right of first refusal or matching right in favor of, Licensor." No residual obligation on Licensee to disclose third-party offers or extend matching/best terms to Licensor survives in the operative text, and the rationale confirms the fee articles (Article V tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) contain no Licensee best-price undertaking.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: after the redline there is no Customer MFN or matching obligation at all, so the product-scope limitation has nothing to bite on and is vacuously satisfied by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the term limit is inapplicable because the operative language leaves no Customer-side MFN/right-to-match running for any period (the former "During the term of this Agreement" trigger is deleted).

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no comparison mechanic remains to be carved out, since the bona fide third-party offer disclosure and same-terms matching right have been removed in full.

elements.element: Minimality \u2013 scope of changes beyond the checklist
elements.evidence: Beyond deleting the matching mechanic, the redline inserts an affirmative transfer permission ("Licensee may sell all or substantially all of its assets, or engage in any merger or consolidation, with any third party without notice to ... Licensor") and retains an unconditional "Licensee shall have the right to consummate any such transaction," duplicating the same permission twice and adding rights outside the MFN checklist.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on its single element: the Article XXII right-of-first-refusal/right-to-match obligation burdening Licensee is removed and expressly negated, and no other Licensee best-terms undertaking exists in the fee articles.

Minimality fails: the checklist required only deletion of the Customer-side matching obligation. The new sentence goes further by granting Licensee an affirmative right to sell all or substantially all assets or merge with any third party "without notice to" Licensor \u2014 a substantive transfer permission outside the MFN checklist. Repair by limiting the insertion to a negation of the matching right (e.g. "Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match any third-party offer.") or by deleting Article XXII outright.

Minimality also fails for duplicate operative coverage: the retained sentence "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate any such transaction" now says the same thing as the new first sentence. The retained sentence had meaning only as the tail of the deleted Exercise Period mechanic; it should be struck rather than conformed.

Preserves intent fails: the drafter expressly leaves Article XX's Change of Control consent regime and Article XXIV(c) assignment consent in place, yet the new Article XXII permits any merger or asset sale "without notice to" Licensor and gives Licensee an unconditional right to consummate. That is a direct contradiction with the retained consent/notice requirements. Repair by (a) removing the "without notice to" and affirmative-permission language, or (b) subordinating the sentence with an express "Subject to Article XX and Article XXIV(c)" qualifier.

Note also that the deleted defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" are confirmed to appear nowhere else, so no dangling cross-reference arises from the deletion itself; the intent defect is the contradiction with the retained change-of-control regime, not an orphan reference.
